title: A pilgrimage
hookLine: a journey to a holy place, near or far
tomorrow: what do you call a birthday you can't remember?

cards: A maps app will always offer the fastest route. Nobody on a pilgrimage wants it. People walk for days to a holy place that a car could reach in an hour.
And Christians honestly disagree about whether the place itself matters. So, does God care which road you walk to pray? Two answers, both from the Bible, and both still walked.

teach.h: VIEW ONE: THE ROAD IS PART OF IT.
teach.b: The first answer: the place matters, and so does the road. Luke says Jesus' family made the trip: “Now his parents went to Jerusalem every year at the feast of the passover.”
A psalm sings the setting out: “I was glad when they said unto me, Let us go into the house of the LORD.”

teach.h: IN WHOSE HEART ARE THE WAYS.
teach.b: Another psalm blesses the ones whose hearts are already traveling: “Blessed is the man whose strength is in thee; in whose heart are the ways of them.”
Pilgrimage is a living custom for Catholic and Orthodox Christians, and for others too: Jerusalem, Rome, saints' shrines, the walking routes to Santiago in Spain. The going is part of the prayer.
The second answer: no spot is holier than another. A woman at a well asks Jesus which mountain is the right one for worship.
He says, “the hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father.”

teach.h: VIEW TWO: IN SPIRIT AND IN TRUTH.
teach.b: And: “God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth.” Some Christians, including some Protestants, hold to this and stay wary of calling one place holy ground.
Now the detail both sides keep, worth telling a friend: two disciples walking home to Emmaus, sad and arguing, and “Jesus himself drew near, and went with them.”
No shrine at the end. A road, and company on it.

how: Catholic and Orthodox Christians, and others too, make pilgrimages to Jerusalem, Rome, saints' shrines or long walking routes such as the one to Santiago; others walk to somewhere close, like the church where they were baptized, while some Christians prefer not to treat any one place as holier.

o: a journey to a holy place where the going is part of prayer
a move overseas to start a new church far from home
a long vacation to rest after a busy church season

games.q: two answers, one road — tap the pairs.
p: let us go into the house of the LORD
in whose heart are the ways

s: some Christians, including some Protestants, are wary of calling one place holier than another.
Luke says Jesus' parents went to Jerusalem every year for Passover
"Now his parents went to Jerusalem every year at the feast of the passover."
in John 4, Jesus names the one right mountain for worship
he says the hour comes for neither this mountain nor Jerusalem: in spirit and in truth.

games.q: a guy at your retreat says, "God's everywhere, so walking to a chapel is pointless." give the pilgrim's best answer.
o: the chapel is the one place where God can really hear you.
the psalms bless a heart set on the road; the going is part of the prayer.
walking lowers stress, so it's good for you either way.
games.why: the pilgrim's best case is Psalm 84: blessed are those in whose heart are the ways. his best case is John 4: spirit and truth. both still walk, like the Emmaus road.

practice: Walk slowly for about a minute, across a room or down a hallway and back, letting each step land before the next. If you pray, let the walking be the prayer; if not, let it be attention.
Then sit for the rest of the time, and feel the place you've come to.

wordCard.voice: A pilgrimage. A journey to a holy place, near or far, where the going is part of the prayer.

orig.note: Hebrew: a song of ascents, the heading over Psalm 122 (the KJV says 'A Song of degrees').

carryVoice: Your line: walk to pray. Some walk toward a holy place, and some just find company on the road. Until tomorrow.
